label: Databricks
headline: Databricks Cheat Sheet
description: Quick reference for Databricks — from Delta Lake and PySpark DataFrames to Unity Catalog, MLflow, magic commands, and cluster configuration.

items.name: %sql
items.syntax:
%sql
SELECT * FROM my_catalog.my_schema.orders LIMIT 10;
items.definition: Run a SQL cell in any notebook language context. Results display as a table automatically.

items.name: %python / %scala / %r
items.syntax:
%python
df = spark.table('orders')
df.show(5)
items.definition: Switch the language of a single cell, overriding the notebook default.

items.name: %fs
items.syntax:
%fs ls /mnt/my-storage/
%fs mkdirs /mnt/my-storage/output/
%fs rm -r /mnt/my-storage/tmp/
items.definition: Run Databricks File System (DBFS) commands. Shorthand for dbutils.fs calls.

items.name: %sh
items.syntax:
%sh
pip install great_expectations
cat /etc/hosts
items.definition: Execute shell commands on the driver node. Changes are local to the driver and not persisted across restarts.

items.name: %run
items.syntax: %run ./utils/helpers
items.definition: Execute another notebook inline — variables and functions defined there become available in the current notebook.

items.name: %md
items.syntax:
## Section Title
Explain what this cell does.
items.definition: Render Markdown in the notebook for documentation. Supports headers, bold, code blocks, and tables.

items.name: CREATE TABLE (Delta)
items.syntax:
CREATE TABLE my_catalog.my_schema.orders (
  order_id BIGINT,
  customer_id BIGINT,
  amount DOUBLE,
  order_date DATE
)
USING DELTA
LOCATION 'abfss://container@storage.dfs.core.windows.net/orders/';
items.definition: Create a managed or external Delta table. Delta is the default format in Databricks — ACID transactions, versioning, and schema enforcement built in.

items.name: MERGE INTO (upsert)
items.syntax:
MERGE INTO orders AS target
USING updates AS source
ON target.order_id = source.order_id
WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET *
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT *;
items.definition: Upsert — update matching rows and insert new ones atomically. The most common CDC pattern in Delta Lake.

items.name: Time Travel
items.definition: Query any previous version of a Delta table. History is retained until VACUUM removes old files.

items.name: DESCRIBE HISTORY
items.syntax: DESCRIBE HISTORY orders;
items.definition: Show all versions of a Delta table — who changed it, when, and what operation was run.

items.name: OPTIMIZE
items.syntax:
OPTIMIZE orders;
OPTIMIZE orders ZORDER BY (customer_id, order_date);
items.definition: Compact small files into larger ones to improve read performance. ZORDER co-locates related data for faster filtering.

items.name: VACUUM
items.syntax: VACUUM orders RETAIN 168 HOURS;
items.definition: Remove old data files no longer referenced by any table version. Default retention is 7 days (168 hours). Do not set below 7 days with concurrent reads.

items.name: RESTORE
items.syntax:
RESTORE TABLE orders TO VERSION AS OF 3;
RESTORE TABLE orders TO TIMESTAMP AS OF '2024-01-15';
items.definition: Roll back a Delta table to a previous version. Creates a new entry in the table history.

items.name: Read data
items.syntax:
df = spark.read.format('delta').load('/mnt/data/orders')
df = spark.read.csv('/mnt/data/file.csv', header=True, inferSchema=True)
df = spark.table('my_catalog.my_schema.orders')
items.definition: Load data into a DataFrame from Delta, CSV, Parquet, JSON, or any registered table.

items.name: Select & filter
items.syntax:
from pyspark.sql.functions import col

df.select('order_id', 'amount') \
  .filter(col('amount') > 100) \
  .show(10)
items.definition: Chain select and filter transformations. Spark is lazy — nothing executes until an action like show() or write is called.

items.name: withColumn
items.syntax:
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, lit, when

df = df.withColumn('tax', col('amount') * 0.2)
df = df.withColumn('tier', when(col('amount') > 500, 'high').otherwise('low'))
items.definition: Add or replace a column using an expression. Use when/otherwise for conditional logic.

items.name: GroupBy & aggregate
items.syntax:
from pyspark.sql.functions import sum, avg, count

df.groupBy('region') \
  .agg(
    sum('amount').alias('total'),
    avg('amount').alias('avg'),
    count('*').alias('orders')
  ).show()
items.definition: Group rows and compute aggregates. Import functions from pyspark.sql.functions — not Python builtins.

items.name: Join
items.syntax: result = orders.join(customers, on='customer_id', how='left')
items.definition: Join two DataFrames. how can be 'inner', 'left', 'right', 'outer', 'semi', or 'anti'.

items.name: Window functions
items.syntax:
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from pyspark.sql.functions import rank, lag

w = Window.partitionBy('region').orderBy(col('amount').desc())
df = df.withColumn('rank', rank().over(w))
items.definition: Apply ranking, lag/lead, and running totals per partition without collapsing rows.

items.name: Write data
items.syntax:
df.write \
  .format('delta') \
  .mode('overwrite')  # or 'append', 'merge'
  .partitionBy('order_date') \
  .saveAsTable('my_catalog.my_schema.orders_out')
items.definition: Persist a DataFrame as a Delta table. Use partitionBy on high-cardinality filter columns to improve query pruning.

items.name: Run SQL
items.syntax: spark.sql('SELECT region, SUM(amount) FROM orders GROUP BY region').show()
items.definition: Execute SQL from Python using spark.sql(). Returns a DataFrame you can chain further transformations on.

items.name: Create temp view
items.syntax:
df.createOrReplaceTempView('orders_view')
# Use in SQL
spark.sql('SELECT * FROM orders_view LIMIT 10').show()
items.definition: Register a DataFrame as a temporary SQL view scoped to the current Spark session.

items.name: CREATE TABLE AS SELECT
items.syntax:
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE my_schema.summary
USING DELTA AS
SELECT region, SUM(amount) AS total
FROM orders
GROUP BY region;
items.definition: Create a new Delta table populated from a query result in one statement.

items.name: Three-level namespace
items.syntax:
-- catalog.schema.table
SELECT * FROM my_catalog.sales.orders;
items.definition: Unity Catalog adds a catalog layer above schemas. All object references use the three-level format.

items.name: CREATE CATALOG
items.syntax:
CREATE CATALOG IF NOT EXISTS prod_catalog
  COMMENT 'Production data';
items.definition: Create a top-level catalog. Each workspace can access multiple catalogs governed by Unity Catalog.

items.name: GRANT privilege
items.definition: Grant fine-grained access on catalogs, schemas, tables, or views. Always grant USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA alongside object-level grants.

items.name: Data lineage
items.syntax:
-- Automatic — view in Catalog Explorer UI
-- Filter by table name → Lineage tab
items.definition: Unity Catalog automatically tracks column-level data lineage across notebooks, jobs, and SQL queries.

items.name: Cluster types
items.syntax:
All-purpose cluster  → interactive notebooks, shared
Job cluster          → single job, auto-terminated
SQL warehouse        → SQL analytics, BI tools
items.definition: All-purpose clusters are billed per hour and shared. Job clusters start fresh for each run and are cheaper for automated pipelines. SQL warehouses are optimised for SQL workloads.

items.name: Spark config (notebook)
items.syntax:
spark.conf.set('spark.sql.shuffle.partitions', '200')
spark.conf.get('spark.sql.shuffle.partitions')
items.definition: Override Spark settings at runtime. Lower shuffle partitions for small datasets (default 200 is too high for most cases).

items.name: Adaptive Query Execution
items.syntax:
-- Enabled by default in DBR 7.3+
spark.conf.set('spark.sql.adaptive.enabled', 'true')
items.definition: AQE dynamically adjusts join strategies, coalesces small partitions, and handles skew at runtime.

items.name: dbutils.secrets
items.syntax: token = dbutils.secrets.get(scope='my-scope', key='api-token')
items.definition: Retrieve secrets from Databricks Secret Scopes (backed by Azure Key Vault or Databricks). Never hardcode credentials in notebooks.

items.name: Start a run
items.syntax:
import mlflow

with mlflow.start_run():
  mlflow.log_param('lr', 0.01)
  mlflow.log_metric('accuracy', 0.95)
  mlflow.sklearn.log_model(model, 'model')
items.definition: Log parameters, metrics, and artefacts to an MLflow experiment. Runs are tracked automatically in the Databricks UI.

items.name: Autologging
items.syntax:
mlflow.autolog()  # before model.fit()
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
items.definition: Automatically log parameters, metrics, and the model for supported frameworks (sklearn, XGBoost, PyTorch, etc.).

items.name: Register model
items.syntax:
mlflow.register_model(
  model_uri='runs:/<run_id>/model',
  name='my-churn-model'
)
items.definition: Add a trained model to the MLflow Model Registry for versioning, staging, and production promotion.

items.name: Load model
items.syntax: model = mlflow.sklearn.load_model('models:/my-churn-model/Production')
items.definition: Load a registered model by name and stage. Swap stages without changing code.

items.name: Create job (UI)
items.syntax:
Workflows → Create Job → Add task
  Task type: Notebook / Python script / dbt / SQL
  Cluster: Job cluster (recommended)
  Schedule: Cron or triggered
items.definition: Jobs orchestrate one or more tasks with dependencies, retries, and alerts. Use job clusters to keep costs predictable.

items.name: Task dependencies
items.syntax:
Task A → Task B → Task C
             ↘ Task D
items.definition: Define a DAG of tasks. A downstream task starts only when all its upstream tasks succeed.

items.name: dbutils.notebook.run
items.definition: Run another notebook programmatically and pass parameters. Returns the value of dbutils.notebook.exit().
